title: The wrong-coloured bishop: another file or a second pawn
outcomes: Predicts what changes when the pawn is not a rook pawn, or when a second pawn is added, and states the claim before checking it
Distinguishes a second pawn on the same file, on another file and on the far wing in verified examples
Writes down which claim was checked by the tablebase and which is only a rule of thumb

steps.text: You know the rook-pawn corner draw from **The wrong bishop: a rook pawn that cannot win** and the family reading from **The wrong-coloured bishop: win or draw from the family**. Now change one thing: a pawn on another file, or a second pawn. Predict the result, say the claim in one sentence, then compare with the checked result. Start with the base case.

steps.caption: White to move, with pawns on a5 and b5. Predict first, then step through.

line.say: Ka7: the king stays in front of the pawns.
Ba3: the bishop takes up the diagonal.
Ka8: the king goes back to the corner.
Kb8: the king steps along the back rank.

steps.text: **Conditions.** In these examples a second pawn on the same file leaves the draw; a second pawn on another file wins, and so does a pawn on the far wing. Rule of thumb: ask which pawns can reach a file the corner king does not guard. One pawn that is not a rook pawn does not have the edge of the board to hide behind, and the single-pawn items below win. That does not make every such position a win: check each one. Verified for these positions only.

steps.title: Add or move one thing
steps.prompt: The base position is a draw. Predict each variant, then check: a second pawn on the same file, a second pawn on the b-file, and the white king one step to the right.

For one position write your claim in a sentence: the files of the pawns, whether the bishop covers the queening corner, and where the defending king is. Then compare with the checked result. The app shows checked results; it does not look anything up for you while you play.
